summary:
Re-review of phase B resubmission sub-mv1hokge-01004365 (112 artifacts; responds to rev-mv1hc5zg-01a3fc75). Every check below was re-run on the final tree after the resubmission.

PB-1 is fixed in src/db/connection.js:
- The journal mode is read first; the WAL switch and the opening pragmas are wrapped in retryWhileBusy. That loop is bounded (budget max(busy timeout, 1 s)), backs off with jitter from 2 to 50 ms, retries only SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED, rethrows any other error at once, and closes the handle on failure.
- My strict race check passes with 0 failures in 20 sequential and 60 parallel runs (ev:ev-mv1hrnhg-017cd4f0).
- The new open-race regression and the RS-14 busy tests pass 10 of 10 repeated runs (ev:ev-mv1hu6ju-01ddc12e).
- npm test passes 370/370 (ev:ev-mv1hqgk1-01c28d5d).
- Each task's declared command passes: b1 177/177 (ev:ev-mv1hul1f-017e688f), b2 110/110 (ev:ev-mv1hvui4-01910b1f), b4 9/9 (ev:ev-mv1hvurz-0103d44f), b3 370/370 plus clean checkout (ev:ev-mv1hwlgh-010ebdc4).

PB-2: all six tests now carry their ids.
PB-3: the follow-ups FU-1..FU-7 name an owning task each in .eccode/artifacts/plan/followups.md.
The artifact list covers all 110 files owned by phase-B tasks (ev:ev-mv1hv48h-019aa8d3).
My independent checks still pass (ev:ev-mv1hwly3-01ca7688): migrations equal the spec, both CSP strings match, scripts match, and the planner agrees with my brute force on RS-FIX-1 and on 3000 random catalogs.

One info note (PB-4) is left for c6's RS-14 busy-timeout-0 test setup. No security-reviewer draft existed when this was written.

findings.title: RS-14 busy-timeout-0 integration test must start the server before taking the lock
findings.detail: main.js applies the migrations at startup inside db.tx, which uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE. With RS_DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=0, a server that starts while another process holds the write lock gets SQLITE_BUSY in that transaction; only openDb's pragmas are retried. c6's rs14-db-busy test should therefore start the server first, then let the lock holder take BEGIN IMMEDIATE, then call reserve. Otherwise it fails at startup rather than proving the 503.
findings.recommendation: c6-reserve-concurrency-browser: order the rs14-db-busy steps as server up, then lock held, then reserve; the delivery lead may add this to followups.md.

resolvedFindings.resolution: openDb reads the journal mode, then wraps the WAL switch and the opening pragmas in retryWhileBusy. The loop is bounded (budget max(busy timeout, 1 s)), backs off with jitter from 2 to 50 ms, retries only SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED, rethrows other errors at once, and closes the handle on failure. A regression test covers it with a 25 x 4-process stress run and a bounded give-up against a real lock holder. My strict race check passes 0/80, the new timing tests pass 10/10, and npm test passes 370/370.

The six tests are renamed with their ids: ARCH-26 (limits.test.js:40), SEC-10 (limits.test.js:66), SEC-12 (hosts.test.js:116), SEC-3 for the RS_TEST_HOOKS row (secrets.test.js:159), RS-14 (connection.test.js:119) and ARCH-25 (app.test.js:310). They pass in the b1 run.

followups.md records each PB-3 item with an owning task and a test-named resolution: FU-1 c2 (PLANNER_LIMIT mapped to a catalogued error), FU-2 d3 (60 s upload deadline), FU-3 c5 then g1 (SPEC_MISMATCH display decision), FU-4 b2/c6 (seed constant vs fixture). It also adds FU-5..FU-7 for PB-1 regressions, the seed hash format and the derive input shape. The orchestrator passes these to the implementers and the phase reviewers check them. That is acceptable while the approved plan stays frozen.
